metadata.description: Robustness boundary for V10 quasi-passive rolling foot gait under terrain roughness and impulse perturbations
metadata.data_source: v11_basin_results.csv scan with 15x15 grid (amplitude x impulse)
metadata.note: Based on documented claims in VERSIONS.md line 15. Boundary determined from 3-trial success/failure classification.

amplitude_range.description: Terrain roughness amplitude (height variation along forward direction)

impulse_range.description: Single lateral impulse force applied at t=4.0s

robustness_boundary.description: Maximum perturbation levels where gait remains stable
robustness_boundary.confidence: Based on 3-trial validation per grid point

flat_terrain_stable_impulse.description: On flat terrain, stable up to 17.1N impulse

rough_terrain_no_impulse.description: Without impulse, stable up to 25.7mm terrain amplitude

critical_amplitude.description: First amplitude level showing partial failures (2/3 success) at impulse=17.1N

critical_impulse.description: All trials fail (0/3 success) at this impulse level across all amplitudes tested

fall_down.description: Loss of stability leading to collapse

stuck.description: Immobilization without falling (not observed in this scan)

key_findings.1_small_perturbation_success: V10 quasi-passive gait tolerates small terrain roughness (amp ≤ 28.6mm) and moderate impulses (imp ≤ 17.1N)
key_findings.2_clear_failure_boundary: Sharp transition from stable to unstable at documented boundary values
key_findings.3_combined_robustness: Controller maintains stability under simultaneous terrain and impulse perturbations within boundary
key_findings.4_failure_mechanism: Large perturbations break the limit cycle and cause fall_down within 4-8 steps

reporting_guidance.academic_integrity: Report as 'small-amplitude terrain success, strong perturbation failure boundary clearly defined'
reporting_guidance.classification: Quasi-passive gait with active hip/knee stabilization (NOT pure passive)
reporting_guidance.honest_representation: Do not overstate robustness - this is the failure boundary, not unlimited tolerance
